what_happened: The person running Athena deleted the finished writer build folder of job 20261027-054305-mgvj (the email-check job) by hand. The job was held on low disk, not failed, so the new low-disk hold worked. Free space stayed at 9.9 GB against the 10 GB gate. The held job's own build was the only thing left to reclaim, and the cleanup cannot reclaim a held job's own writer build. Deleting it let the job resume. No acceptance criterion or check had failed. It was an environment stop.
cause: Athena still has no disk lifecycle. The hold keeps a low-disk job from failing, but it frees nothing. A finished writer build is regenerable, yet nothing reclaims it, counts it against a disk budget, or removes it before the checks. The hold also only makes the job wait, and a held job's own build is the one thing blocking its resume. So the the person running Athena still has to free space by hand. The fix (remove the writer build before checks) is an ordinary queued job and has not been made urgent, although this gap has caused many hand cleanups in a few days.
prevention: Make Athena own the disk lifecycle. It should delete a job's finished writer build folder as soon as the producer's diff and report are saved, before the free-space gate and the checks, and do the same for a held job (the held job's writer build counts as reclaimable). Verify-side builds and caches should be reclaimed in the same way. If free space is still under the gate after all regenerable space is reclaimed, hold the job and show the amount missing. Landing the 'remove the writer build before checks' fix and giving it top priority would close the whole class.
proposed_request: Make Athena reclaim its own build space so low-disk jobs never need a hand cleanup. Outcome: (1) as soon as a producer finishes and its diff and report are saved, Athena removes that job's writer build folder before the free-disk gate and the checks run; (2) when a job is held on low disk, Athena reclaims everything regenerable first, including the held job's own writer build, and resumes the job on its own once free space is above the 10 GB gate; (3) if space is still short after that, the job stays held and the hold message states how much space is missing and what was reclaimed. Acceptance: a test with a fake low-disk gate shows a job whose only reclaimable space is its own finished writer build is resumed without any manual deletion; a test shows the writer build is removed before the checks start and the saved diff and report are untouched; a test shows a job still short of space stays held with the missing amount stated. Give this request top priority in the queue, because it blocks other jobs.
